title: Minimum Operations to Reduce X to Zero
summary: Given an integer array nums and an integer x, you can perform operations where each operation consists of removing either the leftmost or the rightmost element from nums and subtracting its value from x.
statement: Given an integer array nums and an integer x, you can perform operations where each operation consists of removing either the leftmost or the rightmost element from nums and subtracting its value from x. Determine the minimum number of such operations required to reduce x to exactly zero, or return -1 if it is impossible to achieve.
constraints: Positive nums with length up to 100,000.
Remove a prefix and suffix whose sum is exactly x; minimize the total removed length.
hints: Removing ends leaves one contiguous middle window.
Maximize the length of a positive-number window summing to total-x.
Slide a window, shrinking while its sum exceeds the target; convert longest kept length to removals.
Every prefix-plus-suffix removal corresponds uniquely to its remaining middle window, so maximizing kept elements minimizes operations.
editorial: Every prefix-plus-suffix removal corresponds uniquely to its remaining middle window, so maximizing kept elements minimizes operations.

tests.explanation: Removing two values from the right subtracts five.
No combination of end removals sums to four.
